scope: New idle PWM owner implementation review, independent of earlier transport approvals. Read-only production sources; all snapshots, builds and probes confined to .cache/engine/idle-owner-review. No subagents, external service messages, source edits or hardware execution.
verdict: Current source/native owner recheck passes after three actionable findings were fixed. This does not approve the new target ELF: final target build, ISR closure and stack/latency evidence are explicitly pending.

findings.finding: Unconditional common all_low called PwmExecutor.stop on every already-low Stopped command, resetting quiet recovery before the next supervised zero could accumulate20ms. An idle fault could therefore permanently prevent clean stopped recovery.
findings.fix: Both owners stop an active/high PWM; an already-low PWM only receives an electrical low request, preserving supervised-zero continuity. Ordinary unsupervised/live/malformed requests and zero gaps still reset recovery in submit.
findings.evidence: owner_recheck.json: master-off/master-on PWM fault recovery succeeds and core recovers exactly once; guard_probe.json verifies all interruption/gap cases.

findings.finding: A stale phase-context command can be inhibited by the engine executor without a latched TimingStats fault. Deriving PWM enable from the original proposer plus fault-free stats could immediately re-enable idle after the common cut.
findings.fix: pwm_command requires the effective accepted executor command, matching sequence/tune/sensor/configuration epoch and no effective output faults. Both owners pass current_command; recovery also requires accepted context.
findings.evidence: owner_recheck.json: phase-context wait cannot re-enable idle. guard_probe.json: six effective identity/fault/config-hold mismatches inhibit PWM.

findings.finding: At a100% duty cycle boundary, engine_next_time advertised work but engine_pop returned0 because no GPIO edge occurred. Existing drain callers treated the due work as missing or stopped draining, creating false lateness/faults.
findings.fix: The native owner returns explicit0x40000 timer-progress. EngineRuntime returns(-1,False,0,0); compared-controller and Simulation drains skip this marker and continue. It is not a channel8 edge.
findings.evidence: owner_probe.json reproduces code0 at10000us; owner_recheck.json returns262144, retains the high with exactly one rise/no fall, then at20000us returns real channel8 low and common cut on expiry. marker-wrapper-probe.json checks Python marker conversion.

explicit_assessments.master_enabled_stopped_recovery: Enabled master does not enable PWM while the effective engine output is Stopped. Both master settings pass repeated fresh stopped recovery; ordinary live demand never clears a latch.
explicit_assessments.stopped_DFCO: A zero high request cuts immediately and cancels PWM deadlines. DFCO/overrun controller demand is zero while engine spark scheduling may continue. Stopped effective proposals remain disabled and can be supervised recovery commands after raw inputs are quiet.
explicit_assessments.common_all_low: Engine stop/trip, configuration and hardware supervision share the ninth-channel low path. Active/high PWM is stopped immediately. Idle faults trip timing::Cause::IdlePwm, cutting the common owner. Already-low repeats preserve recovery continuity without permitting a high.
explicit_assessments.deadline_heartbeat: PWM uses min(command_us,sampled_us)+20000, checked before heartbeat acceptance. Fresh command at exact expiry cannot rescue an old high. The shared alarm is the minimum of engine and PWM alarms; engine producer progress remains a separate5ms guard and does not extend PWM command freshness.
explicit_assessments.cycle_latching: Pending identity/duty is latched at a scheduled cycle boundary. Zero requests cut immediately. Full duty stays high across boundaries, now exposing progress separately from edges. Scheduled phase carries forward rather than accumulating IRQ lateness.
explicit_assessments.channel8: PWM has independent bool/state and one-pin IO. Core injector/coil masks and high-limit loops remain0..7. Native real idle edges use channel8; timer progress uses-1, never an eighth-bit shift or fabricated GPIO transition.
explicit_assessments.locking_IRAM: All target PWM mutation and common alarm selection occur on the existing target lock shared with ISR. Controller math and period/duty conversion are task-side. PWM dispatch/boundary/level/stop/trip and owner hooks use ECU_ISR_CODE and fixed DRAM state, with integer dispatch. New linked IRAM/literal closure and stack usage must still be checked after the final build.
explicit_assessments.physical_compile_gates: Default idle physical policy is0. Idle physical enable without engine dummy policy fails preprocessing; selected N16R8 fails even with both dummy policies. Generic explicit engine+idle dummy policy compiles. GPIO3 writes/initialization are under ECU_IDLE_DUMMY_LOADS; SAFE/J3/armed checks gate physical highs. No physical routing/valve/eFuse claim follows.

probes.sanitizers: ASan+UBSan, -O1 -g -Wall -Wextra -Werror -fno-omit-frame-pointer. Native owner source included unchanged from copied snapshot; no global cache/library rebuild used.

limits: No target ISR execution or final idle-owner ELF review in this pass. No GPIO/valve, PWM jitter, latency, watchdog physical behavior, task stack high-water or heap minimum measurement.
Root is still implementing broader UI/plant/reference paths. This review checks marker consumption at its explicit drain sites, not full plant/UI integration.
Native CPU/peripheral latency is zero in the model; actual25us PWM lateness behavior and the shared ISR budget need final static and hardware evidence.
